Rashi on Menachot 92b:10:1.hebrew: ולרבינא דאמר גמירי וכו' - לר' שמעון קמבעיא ליה: כיון דא"ר שמעון בבעלים, וגמירי ב' סמיכות בצבור, הא ודאי פשיטא לן דהיינו פר העלם דבר של צבור ושעירי עבודת כוכבים, דהני איתנהו בבעלים, לאפוקי שעיר המשתלח דלא הוי סמיכה בבעלים, דהא לרבי שמעון אין אהרן ובניו מתכפרין בו. ולמה לי קרא לרבות שעירי עבודת כוכבים לסמיכה:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:10:1.english: And according to Ravina, who said it is learned as a tradition, etc. - [The Gemara] is asking according to Rabbi Shimon: Since Rabbi Shimon said [that semichah must be performed] by the owners, and it is learned as a tradition that there are two [instances of] semichah on communal offerings, it is certainly obvious to us that these are the bull for a hidden matter of the community and the he-goats for idol worship, for these are [performed] by the owners—to the exclusion of the scapegoat, where it is not semichah by the owners, since according to Rabbi Shimon, Aaron and his sons do not achieve atonement through it. Why, then, do I need a verse to include the he-goats for idol worship for semichah?

Rashi on Menachot 92b:12:1.hebrew: דאי מקרא - מן החי הוה אמינא, זבחי שלמי צבור טעונים נמי סמיכה מקל וחומר, כדתנן בפרק כל המנחות (לעיל מנחות דף סב:): ומה זבחי שלמי יחיד שאין טעונין תנופה חיין ושחוטין טעונין סמיכה, זבחי שלמי צבור וכו'. והכי קאמר: חי טעון סמיכה באהרן, ולא שלמי צבור טעונין סמיכה באהרן אלא בזקנים, ואיכא שלשה סמיכות בצבור. להכי איצטריך הילכתא, דב' סמיכות בצבור ותו לא:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:12:1.english: For if from scripture - From [the word] "the live [goat]," I would have said that communal peace-offerings also require semikhah through an a fortiori inference (kal vachomer), as we learned in the chapter "Kol HaMenachot" (above, Menachot 62b): "Just as the peace-offerings of an individual, which do not require waving alive and slaughtered, require semikhah, communal peace-offerings etc." And this is what [the verse] means: [Only] the live [goat] requires semikhah by Aaron, but communal peace-offerings do not require semikhah by Aaron, rather by the elders; and [so] there would be three instances of semikhah in communal offerings. Therefore, the halakha was necessary [to teach] that there are two instances of semikhah in communal offerings, and no more.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:15:1.hebrew: לא ידעינן הי נינהו - אותן ב' סמיכות, אי דזבחי שלמי צבור, אי דעבודת כוכבים. קמ"ל אידך קרא: "השעיר", לרבות שעירי עבודת כוכבים, דומיא דשעיר נשיא, לאפוקי זבחי שלמי צבור, דלא דומיא דשעיר נשיא הוא. ואי כתב "השעיר", ה"א סמיכת שעירי עבודת כוכבים באהרן הוא. להכי איצטריך "החי", למימר דחי טעון סמיכה באהרן, ולא שעירי עבודת כוכבים טעונין סמיכה באהרן אלא בזקנים. האי דאמר ר"ש במתני' "אף שעירי עבודת כוכבים" - לאו משום דקסבר שלשה סמיכות בצבור, אלא קסבר שעירי עבודת כוכבים טעונין סמיכה, כאלו: פר העלם דבר של צבור ושעיר המשתלח. ולעולם ב' סמיכות בעינן בצבור בבעלים עצמן ולא בכהנים, דהיינו פר העלם דבר ושעירי עבודת כוכבים:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:15:1.english: We would not know which they are - [Regarding] those two [instances of] semikhah: whether [they include that] of communal peace-offerings, or that of [the goats of] idol worship. The other verse comes to teach us: “the goat” [Leviticus 4:24], to include the goats of idol worship, similar to the goat of a ruler [nasi]; to exclude communal peace-offerings, which are not similar to the goat of a ruler. And if [the verse] had written [only] “the goat,” I would say that the semikhah of the goats of idol worship is [performed] by Aaron. For this reason, “the live [goat]” [Leviticus 16:21] was necessary, to say that the live goat [the scapegoat] requires semikhah by Aaron, but the goats of idol worship do not require semikhah by Aaron, but rather by the elders. As for that which Rabbi Shimon said in the mishna, “also the goats of idol worship” - it is not because he maintains that there are three [instances of] semikhah in communal offerings; rather, he maintains that the goats of idol worship require semikhah, just as do the bull of a community-wide unwitting sin and the scapegoat. And in truth, [the rule that] two [instances of] semikhah are required for communal offerings [applies to those performed] by the owners themselves and not by priests—which are the bull of a community-wide unwitting sin and the goats of idol worship.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:17:1.hebrew: קרבנו - דתלת קרבנו כתיבי בעניינא דשלמים (ויקרא ז), שלשה מינייהו דריש להו התם לדרשא אחרינא, ושלשה דריש הכא:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:17:1.english: His offering - For three [pairs of] “his offering” are written in the section of peace offerings (Leviticus 7); three of them it expounds there for another exposition, and three it expounds here.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:17:2.english: And not the firstborn - [Meaning, and not that the firstborn is] required to have the placing of hands.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:18:1.hebrew: מעשר - שמקדש לפניו ולאחריו, כדאמר (בכורות דף ס.) קרא לתשיעי עשירי וכו':
Rashi on Menachot 92b:18:1.english: Tithe - That it consecrates [the animals] before it and after it, as it says (Bekhorot 60a): [If] he called the ninth "tenth," etc.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:1:1.hebrew: ואין שעירי עבודת כוכבים טעונין סמיכה באהרן אלא בזקנים - וקשיא דרבי שמעון אדרבי שמעון, דהתם אמר באהרן, והכא אומר בזקנים:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:1:1.english: And the goats brought for idol worship do not require semikhah by Aaron, but rather by the elders - And there is a contradiction between [one statement of] Rabbi Shimon and [another statement of] Rabbi Shimon, for there he said [it is performed] by Aaron, and here he says [it is performed] by the elders.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:20:1.hebrew: איכא למיפרך - דלא הוו צריכי קראי, דאפילו לא מיעט רחמנא מקרבנו לא מצית ילפת משלמים: מה לשלמים — בדין הוא דטעונים סמיכה, שכן טעונין תנופת חזה ושוק; תאמר באלו דאין טעונין תנופה? ולמה לי קראי:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:20:1.english: It can be refuted - That the verses were not necessary, for even if the Merciful One had not excluded [them] with 'his offering' [korbano], you could not have derived [them] from peace offerings: What [is unique] about peace offerings? It is only logical that they require semikhah [laying on of hands], as they require waving of the breast and thigh; would you say [the same] of these, which do not require waving? And [if so,] why do I need verses?

Rashi on Menachot 92b:20:2.hebrew: ודאי לא צריכי קראי, אלא אסמכתא בעלמא. אלא, עיקר קראי למה לי, הואיל ואסמכתא נינהו:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:20:2.english: Certainly, verses are not needed [to exclude these offerings], but are a mere support. Rather, [the Gemara asks:] what are the verses primarily needed for, since they are [only] a support?

Rashi on Menachot 92b:2:1.hebrew: והאמר סמיכה בבעלים - ובעלים דשעירי עבודת כוכבים היינו זקנים, ולא כהנים:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:2:1.english: But didn't he say that placing hands [must be done] by the owners - And the owners of the goats [brought for] idol worship are the elders, and not priests.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:4:1.hebrew: והכי קאמר ליה - רבי שמעון לרבי יהודה: מפר לא משמע ליה דממעט עבודת כוכבים, דפר צריך לגופיה, ודאי שעירי עבודת כוכבים טעונים סמיכה. ואי שמיע לך מרבך דלא בעי סמיכה, באהרן הוא דמשמע דלא בעי סמיכה ביה אלא בזקני'. ומיעוטא דאהרן לא מהפר אתי, אלא מהחי, כדקאמר דשעיר ממעט שעיר ואין הפר ממעט שעיר. ולהכי קמתרץ בהאי עניינא דהכי קאמר ליה לרבי שמעון וכו', משום דר' יהודה מפיק טעמיה מפר והוא מהדר ליה מהאי. ע"א: מדאיצטריך סמיכה בשעיר המשתלח למעט מבעלים, אלא באהרן בלבד סגי, מכלל דבעלמא, דהיינו שעיר עבודת כוכבים, טעונה סמיכה בבעלים, דהיינו בזקנים, ולא מ"ה:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:4:1.english: And this is what he said to him - Rabbi Shimon [said] to Rabbi Yehuda: From "the bull" it does not imply to him that it excludes [the goats of] idolatry, for the bull is needed for its own law; certainly the goats of idolatry require semikhah. And if you heard from your teacher that it does not require semikhah, it is regarding Aaron that it implies that it does not require semikhah by him, but rather by the elders. And the exclusion of Aaron does not derive from "the bull," but rather from "the living [goat]," as [the Gemara] says: a goat excludes a goat, but a bull does not exclude a goat. And that is why [the Gemara] resolves [the matter] in this manner, that "this is what he said to him..." because Rabbi Yehuda derived his reasoning from "the bull," and he responded to him from this [other verse]. Another explanation: Since semikhah on the scapegoat was necessary [to be stated] to exclude the owners, [teaching] that [semikhah] by Aaron alone is sufficient, it follows by implication that in general — that is, the goat of idolatry — it requires semikhah by the owners, that is, by the elders, and not from this.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:5:1.hebrew: ור' יהודה למה לי למעוטי - שעירי עבודת כוכבים מקראי, מפר ומן החי:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:5:1.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda, why do I need to exclude - The goats of idol worship from the verses: from "the bull" and from "the live [goat]".

Rashi on Menachot 92b:5:2.hebrew: והאמר רבינא גמירי ב' סמיכות בצבור - ותו לא. וכיון דאמר במתני' חוץ מפר העלם דבר של צבור ושעיר המשתלח, היינו ב' סמיכות, ולא צריך קרא למעוטינהו בברייתא מקראי:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:5:2.english: But didn't Ravina say: It is learned as a tradition [that there are] two layings of hands on communal [offerings] - And no more. And since it is stated in the mishna, "except for the bull of an unwitting communal sin and the scapegoat," these are the two layings of hands, and a verse should not be needed to exclude them in the baraita from verses.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:5:3.hebrew: גירסא בעלמא - כלומר, ודאי לא צריך למעוטינהו טפי מקראי, אלא להכי הדר ומעטינהו משום גירסא בעלמא, שתהא רגיל: שתי סמיכות בצבור ותו לא, וקראי אסמכתא בעלמא. ע"א: גירסא בעלמא — ודאי לא צריכי קראי, אלא כך קיבלה רבי יהודה מרבו בלשון זה, כ"ש. ולר' שמעון, אע"ג דמרבה שעירי עבודת כוכבים לסמיכה, אפי' הכי ליכא אלא ב' סמיכות בצבור, דהא גמר ב' סמיכות בצבור לרבי שמעון היינו בבעלים, ושעיר המשתלח אין טעון סמיכה בבעלים, דבני אהרן לרבי שמעון אין מתכפרין בשעיר המשתלח. אבל לר' יהודה, דלא בעי סמיכה בבעלים, איצטריך:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:5:3.english: A mere formulation - That is to say: Certainly it was not necessary to exclude them further from verses; rather, this is why [the Baraita] went back and excluded them: for the sake of a mere formulation, so that you would be accustomed [to reciting]: "Two instances of placing hands for communal [offerings], and no more," and the verses are merely a textual support. Another explanation: "A mere formulation" — Certainly verses are not needed; rather, Rabbi Yehuda received [the tradition] from his teacher in this phrasing; so I heard. And according to Rabbi Shimon, even though he includes the goats of idol worship for placing hands, even so there are only two instances of placing hands for communal [offerings], for that tradition of "two instances of placing hands for communal [offerings]," according to Rabbi Shimon, refers to [placing hands] by the owners; and the scapegoat does not require placing hands by the owners, since according to Rabbi Shimon the sons of Aaron do not achieve atonement through the scapegoat. But according to Rabbi Yehuda, who does not require placing hands [specifically] by owners, it was necessary [to derive the exclusion from a verse].

Rashi on Menachot 92b:6:1.hebrew: ורבי שמעון - דפשיטא ליה דשעירי עבודת כוכבים טעונין סמיכה בזקנים, מנלן:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:6:1.english: And Rabbi Shimon - For it is obvious to him that the he-goats for idolatry require semikhah by the elders — from where do we derive this?

Rashi on Menachot 92b:7:1.english: He derives it from that which was taught: "And he shall lay his hand" - Which is written regarding the he-goat of a ruler [nasi].

Rashi on Menachot 92b:7:2.hebrew: לרבות שעיר נחשון לסמיכה - שהרי הוא נמי שעיר נשיא. ואי קשיא לך: דתנן כל קרבנות היחיד טעונין סמיכה, והאי נמי קרבן יחיד הוא, ולמה לי קרא? אפי' הכי איצטריך קרא לרבויי לסמיכה, דשעה מדורות לא ילפינן:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:7:2.english: To include the goat of Nahshon for semikhah - For it, too, was the goat of a prince. And if you ask: But we learned in a mishna, "All individual offerings require semikhah," and this too is an individual offering, so why do I need a verse? Even so, a verse was needed to include it for semikhah, for we do not derive a temporary [offering] from [those of future] generations.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:7:3.english: And Rabbi Shimon said: To include the goats of idol worship - That they, too, are a goat [requiring] semichah.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:7:4.hebrew: שהיה רבי שמעון אומר וכו' - ושעירי עבודת כוכבים נמי נכנס דמן לפנים, לאפוקי שעיר נחשון דאין דמו נכנס לפנים:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:7:4.english: As Rabbi Shimon would say, etc. - And the blood of the goats for idol worship also enters inside [the Sanctuary], to the exclusion of the goat of Nahshon, whose blood does not enter inside.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:8:1.english: Why do I need [this] - Since Scripture includes it.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:8:2.english: Merely a mnemonic - That [statement]: "Any sin offering whose blood enters..." etc.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:9:1.hebrew: ולר' שמעון - דאמר לרבות שעירי עבודת כוכבים, אימא לרבות שעיר יום הכפורים הנעשה בפנים, דהא נכנס דמו לפנים:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:9:1.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon - Who said [that the verse serves] to include the goats of idol worship, say [rather that it serves] to include the Yom Kippur goat performed inside, for its blood enters inside.

Rashi on Menachot 92b:9:2.hebrew: לא ס"ד דומיא דשעיר נשיא דמכפר על עבירות מצוה ידועה - לאפוקי שעיר הנעשה בפנים, דמכפר על טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, שיש בה ידיעה בתחלה ואין בה ידיעה בסוף:
Rashi on Menachot 92b:9:2.english: It would not enter your mind; [it must be] similar to the goat of a ruler, which atones for transgressions of a known commandment - To exclude the goat whose service is performed inside, which atones for the defilement of the Temple and its sacred items where there was awareness at the beginning, but no awareness at the end.

Tosafot on Menachot 92b:20:1.hebrew: איכא למיפרך - תימה: נילף מהקישא דכל הקרבנות, כדדרשינן (זבחים דף ז:): "ביום צוותו" — זה בכור, מעשר ופסח:
Tosafot on Menachot 92b:20:1.english: This can be refuted - This is difficult: let us derive [that they require placing hands] from the juxtaposition of all the offerings, as we expound (Zevachim 7b): "On the day that He commanded" — this refers to the firstborn, animal tithe, and Paschal offering!

Tosafot on Menachot 92b:20:2.hebrew: שכן טעונין נסכים ותנופת חזה ושוק - וכי תימא: חטאת ואשם יוכיחו? מה לכולהו — דמתן דמים מרובה למזבח, תאמר בהני דבמתנה אחת:
Tosafot on Menachot 92b:20:2.english: For they require libations and waving of the breast and thigh - And if you should say: let a sin-offering and a guilt-offering prove it [that laying on of hands is required even without libations and waving]? What is common to all of them is that the application of their blood to the altar is multiple; can you say [the same] of these, which require only a single application?

Tosafot on Menachot 92b:2:1.hebrew: הא לרבי שמעון סמיכה בבעלים בעינן - ואהרן לאו בעלים הוא. דאי משום שמתכפר עם כל ישראל — הא אמר ר' שמעון במסכת הוריות (דף ה.): פר ושעיר לכל שבט! והא דחשיבי זקנים בעלים, אע"פ שיש פר ושעיר לבית דין בפני עצמן — כיון דעל ידיהן נעשה החטא, קרי להו בעלים:
Tosafot on Menachot 92b:2:1.english: Behold, according to Rabbi Shimon, we require semikhah by the owners - And Aaron is not an owner! For if [one were to suggest that he is considered an owner] because he achieves atonement together with all of Israel — behold, Rabbi Shimon said in tractate Horayot (5a): a bull and a goat for each tribe! And as for the elders being considered "owners" [who perform semikhah], even though there is a bull and a goat for the court on its own — since the sin was brought about through them, they are called "owners."

Tosafot on Menachot 92b:5:1.hebrew: גירסא בעלמא - ל"א פירש בקונטרס, כלומר: דרבי יהודה לית ליה הלכה למשה מסיני בשתי סמיכות, אלא בגירסא בעלמא נקט להו, ויליף להו מקראי. וקשה, דבפרק כל המנחות באות מצה (לעיל מנחות סב:) פריך: ויהו זבחי שלמי צבור טעונין סמיכה מק"ו? ומשני: גמירי שתי סמיכות בצבור. וי"ל, דהתם מיירי לר' שמעון, דאית ליה גמרא, כדאמר נמי בסמוך לרבינא; ורבי יהודה הוה ממעט זבחי שלמי צבור מהפר. עוד פירש לשון אחר: "גירסא בעלמא" - קראי אסמכתא בעלמא, לאוקמי גירסא לסימנא:
Tosafot on Menachot 92b:5:1.english: Merely a recited text - In one explanation, Rashi explained: that is to say, Rabbi Yehuda does not hold that there is a *Halakha le-Moshe mi-Sinai* (law transmitted to Moses from Sinai) regarding two semikhot (layings of hands); rather, he took them merely as a recited tradition, and derived them from verses. And this is difficult: for in the chapter "All Meal-Offerings Come Unleavened" (above, Menachot 62b), the Gemara asks: "Let the communal peace-offerings require semikhah by an a fortiori argument (*kal va-ḥomer*)?" And it answers: "We have a received tradition that there are [only] two semikhot for communal offerings." And one can answer that there, the Gemara is speaking according to Rabbi Shimon, who accepts the received tradition, as is also stated nearby according to Ravina; whereas Rabbi Yehuda would exclude communal peace-offerings from [the verse regarding] "the bull." He also explained another interpretation: "Merely a recited text" — the verses are merely a textual support (*asmakhta*), to establish the recited tradition as a mnemonic.
